description_good.justification: The README at https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity#readme opens by stating what the software does (inventory and governance for non-human identities in AWS accounts) and the problem it addresses.

interact.justification: Issues and pull requests are open on GitHub; https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md states how to propose changes and report problems.

contribution.justification: https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md: every change travels a branch and a pull request through the documented gates.

contribution_requirements.justification: https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md names the gates, the writing rules, and the requirement that counted figures move with the change.

documentation_basics.justification: The README (https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity#readme) documents installation by compose, SQLite, and Kubernetes, use under "Using it", and the full API surface under "How it is put together".

documentation_interface.justification: The routes block in the README is gated by a test against the application's actual route table, and the application serves interactive API documentation from FastAPI at /docs.

repo_track.justification: Git tracks every change; the mainline ruleset requires pull requests.

repo_interim.justification: Every interim change lands as a pull request on the public repository; nothing is batched into releases.

version_unique.justification: Tags of the form v0.x.y, one per release, see the release process recorded in DECISIONS.md (D-050).

version_semver.justification: Semantic versioning, v0.2.0 the current release.

version_tags.justification: Signed tags start the release workflow; https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/tags

release_notes.justification: Each release at https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/releases carries notes generated from the annotated tag message, and the README's "What comes next" section states the roadmap.

release_notes_vulns.justification: No vulnerabilities have needed fixing to date; SECURITY.md commits to naming any fixed vulnerability in the release notes.

report_responses.justification: https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/blob/main/SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgment within seven days and a triage answer within fourteen.

enhancement_responses.justification: Enhancement requests are answered in the issue tracker on the same commitments.

vulnerability_report_process.justification: https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/blob/main/SECURITY.md: private reporting through GitHub security advisories.

build.justification: Dockerfile and docker compose; pip installs with hash-verified requirements.

test.justification: pytest suite of 146 tests, run in continuous integration on every change and on the oldest supported interpreter.

test_invocation.justification: pytest -q, documented in AGENTS.md and in the README under "How it was built and gated".

test_most.justification: Coverage 94 percent over a 90 percent floor enforced in CI, plus a mutation check: seven controls removed one at a time, the suite notices each.

test_policy.justification: AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md require tests for new functionality; counted README figures are recounted by a test so a new test must move the figure.

tests_are_added.justification: Every functional change in the history lands with its tests; the counted figures make an untested addition visible.

warnings.justification: ruff and mypy strict run in continuous integration.

warnings_fixed.justification: The pipeline is clean of warnings; a new warning fails the build.

warnings_strict.justification: mypy strict mode and the full ruff rule set.

know_secure_design.justification: The README sections "How a request is protected" and "What it defends against", and the threat model in SECURITY.md.

know_common_errors.justification: Input handling is documented and tested: escaping at every exit, formula-safe CSV, text-only rendering, parameterized queries.

crypto_published.justification: Argon2id via passlib for passwords; TLS from the platform. No home-grown cryptography.

crypto_call.justification: Only library calls: passlib and the standard library secrets module.

crypto_keylength.justification: Argon2id parameters at library defaults; tokens from secrets.token_urlsafe(32).

crypto_working.justification: No broken algorithms in use; MD5 and SHA-1 appear nowhere.

crypto_pfs.justification: The application terminates no TLS itself; transport security is the deployment platform's.

crypto_password_storage.justification: Argon2id hashing with per-password salts via passlib.

crypto_random.justification: The secrets module for every token.

delivery_mitm.justification: HTTPS delivery, signed tags, and provenance attestations on release assets and the container image.

delivery_unsigned.justification: Build provenance attestations on every release asset, verifiable with gh attestation verify; https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/releases

vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days.justification: No outstanding vulnerabilities; Dependabot alerts and security updates are enabled and reviewed.

static_analysis.justification: CodeQL on every commit and weekly; ruff and mypy strict.

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities.justification: CodeQL security queries for Python and for workflow files.

dynamic_analysis.justification: ClusterFuzzLite fuzzes the two import parsers under AddressSanitizer on every pull request touching them and weekly, alongside property-based tests in the suite.

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions.justification: pytest assertions are active in every run.

test_continuous_integration.justification: GitHub Actions on every push and pull request; ten required checks gate the mainline.

no_leaked_credentials.justification: TruffleHog scans the full history at every commit and in continuous integration, with verification against providers.

english.justification: All documentation and discussion are in English.

maintained.justification: Actively developed: release v0.2.0 in August 2026 with changes merged weekly since, and a stated roadmap in the README.
